title: Glossary
description: Technical terms used in these docs, in alphabetical order.

terms.definition: UI framework used for the launcher.
The basis for SS14's (heavily modified) physics system.
Self-contained versions of the codebase that you can add commits to. The default branch is usually `master` or `main`, but you can make as many as you like.
The game engine for SS13.
The act of switching to another branch so you can edit it or look at its changes locally.
An interface that connects to the command line to run scripts.

A snapshot of the repository's working tree at a given time. Basically a save point. A 'commit' is just a list of files that have been changed from the last commit, and the changes that are 'committed' are the changes that you've 'staged'.
The 'game' running on RobustToolbox.
Convar/Console Variable. Configurable value that you can change in the config files or through the console.
A comparison between two files of lines or information changed.
BYOND/SS13's sprite file format. Converted to an RSI for our usage.
Entity Component System
Entity Unique Identifier
The act of getting the branches and commits of a remote repository, but not actually doing anything with them yet.
A repository that is based on another repository. If you're going to make a pull request to the SS14 repo, you need to fork it first.
An open-source version control software that allows users to make new changes, view different changes, see who made changes, etc. without having to coordinate and tabulate everything themselves.
An online service run by Microsoft that hosts Git repositories for easy collaboration. SS14's main repository is hosted on GitHub.
GUI
Inversion of Control
Networking library.

A file conflict which occurs when integrating changes from one branch into another can't be done automatically, because they both change the same area in a file, or their changes are mutually exclusive in some other way.
The act of integrating the changes from one branch into another branch.
The act of integrating your local changes into a remote repository.
A GitHub-specific action that allow you to request that your local branch and all of its changes be merged into another repository's branch.
The act of integrating changes from a remote repository's branch into your local branch.
Potentially Visible Set. Stops the server from sending out-of-range entities to clients.
A name for and link to a remote repository that your local repository can use.

A folder where you can use Git to make changes and keep track of changes made. Local repositories are repositories you have on your computer, and remote repositories are repositories that live on websites like GitHub. Repositories are made up of a lot of branches.
A crossplatform IDE for C#. (Can be obtained for free for non-commercial use).
Custom game engine on which SS14 is built.
Robust Station Images. SS14's image 'file' format (actually a folder).
The original game that Space Station 14 (SS14) is based on.
Remake of Space Station 13 (SS13).
The act of adding (with the git add command) changes from your working tree into the 'staging area', where you can then commit staged changes to a branch.
A repositories that is located inside another repository.
Tom's Obvious Minimal Language. Like YAML but for config.
Visual Studio Community 2017/19. Not the same as VSC. The IDE for people who can't get a Rider license.
Visual Studio Code. Not the same as VS.
SS14 Server Watchdog. Used for dedicated server logging, updating and general management.
Every file and folder that's in the repository.
YAML Ain't Markup Language. Used to define prototypes.
